subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider text like `LLM error api_error: Internal server error` be classified for cron/fallback behavior?
rationale: The source shows this is not a regex-only bug because each possible reason changes retry matching and whether provider/auth-profile health is affected during cron runs.

options.title: Map to `server_error` with cron-local handling
options.body: Use the existing `server_error` reason for plain provider 500s, keep shared auth-profile cooldown out of the default path, and add tests proving cron fallback/retry/alert timing.

options.title: Map to `overloaded`
options.body: Skip same-provider candidates sooner, but require explicit proof that cron-local policy prevents broad provider-health poisoning during generic HTTP 500 outages.

options.title: Keep timeout semantics
options.body: Leave plain 500s as timeout and solve the missed-window problem with per-candidate or first-progress budgets instead of a new outage classification.

recommendation.title: Map to `server_error` with cron-local handling
recommendation.body: Use the existing `server_error` reason for plain provider 500s, keep shared auth-profile cooldown out of the default path, and add tests proving cron fallback/retry/alert timing.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the closest structured server-error fix and have the strongest recent history on the affected failover/cron classification path.
